message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card: it can be worth either **1 point** or **11 points**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without busting.

**Key points**

| Situation | How the Ace is counted |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace** | Count it as 11 if doing so keeps the total ≤ 21; otherwise count it as 1. |
| **Two Aces** | One Ace is counted as 11 and the other as 1 (so the pair totals 12). |
| **Natural Blackjack** | An Ace + a 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K) = 21. This is called a “blackjack” and usually pays 3:2 unless the dealer also has a blackjack. |
| **Splitting Aces** | If you’re allowed to split a pair of Aces, each Ace is treated as a separate hand. In many casinos you’ll receive only one additional card per Ace (no further hits). |
| **Dealer’s Upcard** | If the dealer shows an Ace, you may be offered a “double down” or “split” depending on the casino rules. |

**Bottom line:**  
An Ace is always counted as 11 unless that would cause your hand to exceed 21, in which case it’s counted as 1. This flexibility is what makes the Ace such a powerful card in Blackjack.
